newsitem.title: USA: Sun Healthcare in deal to buy Regency.
newsitem.headline: Sun Healthcare in deal to buy Regency.

text.p: Sun Healthcare Group Inc said on Sunday that it and Regency Health Services Inc signed a definitive agreement under which Sun will acquire all of the outstanding shares of Regency for $22 per share, or about $369 million in cash.
In addition, about $220 million of Regency debt will be assumed or refinanced, putting the value of the total transaction at about $589 million, Sun said in a statement.
Regency's projected total revenues for 1997 are about $670 million, the statement said.
Regency operates nursing facilities and provides rehabilitation therapy, institutional pharmacy and home health services, it said.
Regency presently operates 116 inpatient facilities (including 46 with subacute specialty units), 26 outpatient rehabilitation therapy clinics and eight institutional pharmacies, the statement said.
Sun said it expects to complete the merger with Regency during the fourth quarter of 1997, and expects the transaction to be accretive in 1998.
Regency has rehabilitation therapy contracts with 202 facilities and pharmacy contracts with 164 facilities, the statement said.

Under the merger agreement, which was unanimously approved by the boards of both companies, Sun will commence a tender offer for all of the outstanding shares of Regency within five business days, Sun said.
Upon completion of the tender offer, the merger agreement provides that shares of Regency not tendered will be acquired in a merger at the same price per share in cash, Sun said.

Smith Management Company and its affiliates, Regency's largest shareholder group, have agreed to tender their shares, which constitute 25 percent of Regency's common stock, pursuant to the tender offer, Sun said.
In addition, certain officers and directors have agreed to tender their shares, Sun said.

Sun said it has obtained a long-term financing commitment of about $1 billion through NationsBank of Texas N.A., the lead lender in Sun's existing credit facility, to provide financing for the Regency acquisition, satisfy outstanding credit facility obligations and provide for ongoing working capital needs, Sun said.
Depending on market conditions, Sun said it subsequently plans to replace a portion of the NationsBank financing through a combination of equity and debt offerings.
The merger will be accounted for on a purchase accounting basis, Sun said.

The offer is subject to the tender of at least a majority of Regency's shares on a fully diluted basis, the consent of a majority of Regency's existing subordinated debt holders, and other customary conditions including required government approvals.
The offer is not subject to Sun's arranging for financing as a condition for closing, Sun said.
No changes will be made to Sun's board of directors and no significant changes are expected to be made to Sun's senior management, the company said.
Considering both acquisitions, Sun expects annualised revenues in excess of $3 billion in 1998, and will employ more than 72,000 people in the United States and the United Kingdom.
Sun said its assimilation of Regency's corporate operations is expected to result in a significant reduction in combined general and administrative expense.
Sun said the addition of Regency's 116 inpatient facilities provides immediate opportunities to expand Sun's pharmacy, medical supply, therapy and ancillary service businesses.
Sun said it expects to leverage its infrastructure and management expertise to achieve enhanced efficiencies and improved operational performance in Regency's contract therapy business.
Sun said the combination of its pharmacy businesses with that of Regency will create significant economies of scale and operating efficiencies.
